---
title: Views, watch time and unique viewers
description: Read how often your videos are watched, for how long and by how many people, counted by ClipMux's delivery with no player beacon.
icon: ChartLine
---

ClipMux counts playback where it serves it. Every view, every segment of
watch time and every byte comes from delivery's own requests, so there is
no analytics script to add to your pages and nothing for a viewer's ad
blocker to stop. Your backend reads the numbers from the API; the server's
owner sees them under **Analytics** in the dashboard.

## Before you start

- An API key with the `analytics:read` scope. Keys don't have it by
  default, including the one `init` makes; the server's owner adds it to a
  new key on the server:

  ```bash
  clipmux admin create-key --app "My app" --scopes uploads:write,assets:read,assets:write,analytics:read
  ```

  The owner can also create one with `POST /v1/apps/{id}/api-keys` and
  `"scopes"` in the body.

- For unique viewers, tokens signed with a viewer ID; see below.

## Read the numbers

<Tabs items={['Node', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node">

```ts
import { ClipMux } from '@clipmux/node'

const clipmux = new ClipMux({ apiKey: process.env.ANALYTICS_API_KEY })

const app = await clipmux.analytics.get('30d') // every video of the key's app
const one = await clipmux.analytics.asset('ast_…', '7d') // one video
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">

```bash
curl -s 'https://video.example.com/v1/analytics?range=30d' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ANALYTICS_API_KEY"
curl -s 'https://video.example.com/v1/analytics/assets/ast_…?range=7d' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ANALYTICS_API_KEY"
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

`range` is `24h`, `7d`, `30d` or `90d`; anything else is
`400 invalid_request`. `GET /v1/analytics` covers the key's own app.
`GET /v1/analytics/assets/{id}` covers one of its videos, and a deleted
video keeps its history.

```json
{
  "totals": { "views": 1840, "watch_seconds": 302400, "unique_viewers": 412, "bytes_delivered": 98123456789 },
  "previous": { "views": 1502, "watch_seconds": 251000, "unique_viewers": null, "bytes_delivered": 80211000000 },
  "series": [{ "t": "2026-11-03T00:00:00Z", "views": 260, "watch_seconds": 43100, "bytes_delivered": 14000000000 }],
  "top_assets": [{ "asset_id": "ast_…", "title": "Lesson 42", "views": 310, "watch_seconds": 61000, "bytes_delivered": 17000000000 }],
  "collecting": { "builtin": true, "edge": "not_used" }
}
```

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `totals` | The range's views, watch time in seconds, unique viewers and bytes. They include deleted videos' history. |
| `previous` | The same for the same length of time immediately before, to show a change. |
| `series` | One bucket per hour for `24h`, per UTC day otherwise, oldest first, with empty buckets as zeros. `t` is the bucket's start. The last bucket is the current one, so it's partial. |
| `top_assets` | Up to 10 live videos, by views. Not in the one-video response. A `title` may be missing. |
| `collecting` | Where counts come from; see [Edge counts](#edge-counts). |

## What counts

- **A view** is one `master.m3u8` served. A player loads the master once
  when it starts, so a view is one play start. A viewer who reloads the page
  makes another view.
- **Watch time** is 6 seconds for each audio segment served (or video
  segment, for a video with no audio). It counts what was fetched, not what
  was watched, so it overcounts by the player's buffer ahead: a viewer who
  stops after 10 seconds may have fetched 30.
- **Bytes** are every body delivery sent.

Only successful answers count; refusals never do. Dashboard previews,
library posters and the server's setup test aren't counted. Plays through
[share links](/docs/build/play/share-links) are.

## Unique viewers

ClipMux doesn't know who your viewers are. To count them, put a stable ID
for each viewer in the playback token's `vid` claim:

```ts
// clipmuxHandler's playback callback
return { viewerId: user.id }

// or when you sign a token yourself
await clipmux.playback.token('pid_…', { viewerId: user.id })
```

For anonymous viewers, use a random ID you keep in their session. ClipMux
stores only a keyed hash of `vid`, never the ID itself. `unique_viewers`
counts distinct viewers on the days the range touches (for `24h`, yesterday
and today), and is `null` when no view in the range carried a `vid`.

Nothing in analytics stores an IP address, User-Agent, referrer, token or
raw viewer ID.

## How long numbers are kept

- Hourly counts, behind the `24h` range: 14 days.
- Daily counts and viewer hashes: 180 days, enough for two `90d` ranges.

Older numbers are deleted.

## Edge counts

With [Cloudflare edge delivery](/docs/self-host/delivery/cloudflare), most
requests never reach the ClipMux server. The Cloudflare Worker counts them
instead, and the server pulls those counts in every 5 minutes once the
owner connects [edge analytics](/docs/self-host/delivery/edge-analytics).
`collecting.edge` says which applies:

| `collecting.edge` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `not_used` | No Cloudflare delivery. The server counts everything. |
| `not_connected` | Cloudflare delivers, but its counts aren't pulled in, so most plays are missing. |
| `connected` | Edge counts are pulled in. The last few minutes appear on the next pull. |

<LeavesYourServers>
  With Cloudflare delivery, Cloudflare serves your viewers, and the Worker
  records each counted request in Cloudflare's Analytics Engine: the
  project, app, video and playback IDs, the kind of request, the views,
  watch time and bytes, and the keyed viewer hash. The ClipMux server reads
  them back with a read-only token.
</LeavesYourServers>

## Check it works

Play a video for a minute with a token that carries a `vid`, then:

```bash
curl -s 'https://video.example.com/v1/analytics/assets/ast_…?range=24h' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ANALYTICS_API_KEY"
```

`totals.views` is at least 1 and `unique_viewers` at least 1. Counts reach
Postgres within about 15 seconds.

- `403 insufficient_scope`: the key lacks `analytics:read`.
- `404 not_found`: the video belongs to another app.
- `unique_viewers` is `null`: no token in the range had a `vid`.
